question: When I flatten a stage to ship a single USD file to third parties, the variant sets get resolved and only the selected variant remains. How can I flatten it and still keep the variant sets, so recipients can switch variants?
expected_facts: Flattening a stage (UsdStage::Export/Flatten, usdcat --flatten) evaluates variants and keeps only the opinions of the currently selected variants.
Flattening a layer stack (usdcat --flattenLayerStack or UsdUtilsFlattenLayerStack) combines the sublayers into a single layer while preserving all other composition arcs, so variant sets survive.

question: On the same prim, are collection-based material bindings stronger than direct bindings? In my experience direct bindings win, but the bound material resolution rules say collection-based bindings are stronger.
expected_facts: If a prim has a direct binding and is directly targeted by a collection binding, the direct binding wins by default.
The bindMaterialAs metadata (strongerThanDescendants) can make a collection-based binding override descendant prim bindings.

question: If I only care about a primvar authored directly on the mesh, can I access it with GetAttribute("primvars:foo") like a normal attribute, or are there cases where I should go through UsdGeomPrimvarsAPI?
expected_facts: Primvars are accessible as attributes.
Indexed primvars keep their indices in a separate attribute (primvars:NAME:indices).
Blocking the primvar attribute directly blocks only the elements, not the indices; UsdGeom.PrimvarsAPI BlockPrimvar() blocks both.

question: In a prim spec's reference list, what is the difference between prepended and appended references, and why does AddReference() produce prepended references?
expected_facts: An appended item goes to the back of the resolved list, so an arc appended in a stronger layer is weaker than same-type arcs appended from weaker layers.
A prepended item goes to the front, so an arc prepended in a weaker layer is still stronger than same-type arcs appended from stronger layers.
The UsdReferences API creates prepended references by default so the reference contributes stronger opinions than references in weaker layers; the position parameter allows other options.

question: When I mark a referenced prim as instanceable, what happens to material bindings and other overrides authored on prims beneath it?
expected_facts: Making a reference instanceable means overrides on prims beneath it, including ones already in the referencing context, are ignored.
With instancing you cannot uniquely override prims beneath the instance root.
Direct material bindings cannot be established for gprims inside instances without breaking the instances.

question: If I query an attribute at a time after its last authored time sample, what value do I get, and which UsdAttribute calls list the times of its authored samples?
expected_facts: Queries outside the authored range return the held value extrapolated from the nearest TimeSample.
UsdAttribute::GetTimeSamples and GetTimeSamplesInInterval return the time coordinates of the attribute's samples.

question: Is there a way to retime a layer or stage with a non-linear frame mapping (for example frame 50 to 100, frame 51 to 102), given that a layer offset only supports a constant offset and scale?
expected_facts: Layer offsets are meant for simple retiming; value clips are the more powerful mechanism for elaborate cases.
An explicit clip set's times metadata is a list of (stageTime, clipTime) pairs that maps stage time to clip time and can scale, offset, loop or reverse clips.

question: Does usdzip have a file size limit? Zipping a very large flattened file produced a 3 GB usdz with no errors, but usdview fails to open it.
Can I extract the textures embedded in a USDZ file, for example to re-export the asset as GLB?
expected_facts: Usdz files can be unpacked using any zip/unzip program.
usdzip can list the contents of a package, and the UsdzFileFormat has helper APIs for introspecting and extracting data from a package.

question: How can I get a list of all available single-apply and multiple-apply API schemas, so a user can pick one from a list and apply it to a prim?
How is a named collection recorded on a prim, and how can I test whether a prim has an applied API schema with a given instance name?
expected_facts: CollectionAPI is a multiple-apply schema; each application has an instance name, which is the collection name.
Applied API schemas are recorded in the prim's apiSchemas metadata and answer presence queries via UsdPrim::HasAPI.
The path-expression predicate hasAPI accepts an instanceName, matching only prims with an applied schema of that instance name.

question: How do I render frames with usdrecord, or with FrameRecorder in Python, without the default camera light that I can turn off in usdview?
Should a dome light be visible as the background by default, and is there a standard way to control its camera visibility separately from its lighting contribution?
What is the UsdPhysicsRigidBodyDesc structure for, and why would I use it instead of reading UsdPhysicsRigidBodyAPI directly?
How do I create nested variant sets (a variant set defined inside a variant) with the Python API?
expected_facts: Nesting is done by nesting the use of edit contexts in code (UsdEditContext / GetVariantEditContext()).
Inside the outer variant's edit context, appending the inner variant set authors it inside the selected outer variant, so its contents can vary per outer variant.

question: What value does a UsdUVTexture output when the texture file it references cannot be read?
expected_facts: UsdUVTexture's fallback input (float4, default (0, 0, 0, 1)) is the value used when the texture cannot be read.

question: If relocates are weaker than local opinions in the LIVRPS strength order, why does my local prim disappear when I author a relocate and flatten the stage?
expected_facts: Relocates can only map prims introduced via composition arcs (a root prim cannot be relocated).
Once a source path is relocated it is no longer valid in the current namespace; local opinions authored at the source path produce an error.

question: How do a camera's focal length, horizontal and vertical aperture, and focus distance relate to what appears in the camera's view?
expected_facts: For a perspective camera the aperture is an axis-aligned rectangle in the plane at the focal length in front of the camera origin.
Aperture and focal length are in 1/10 of the scene world unit.
Focus distance is the distance to the plane of focus and, with focal length and fstop, sets depth of field.

question: How can I make a value clip loop for a cycling animation?
expected_facts: An explicit clip set's times entries can loop a clip, e.g. [(0, 0), (10, 10), (10, 0), (20, 10)] plays it twice.
Templated clip metadata does not support looping.

question: Is there an existing call that lists the layers contributing to a stage, so I don't have to write my own recursive traversal?
expected_facts: UsdStage::GetUsedLayers lets you count and examine the layers required to produce the current view of a stage.
usdzip --asset discovers all recursively referenced files when packaging.

question: A spot light is a SphereLight with ShapingAPI applied. How can I check whether a SphereLight prim has the ShapingAPI schema applied?
expected_facts: Applied API schemas are recorded in the prim's apiSchemas metadata.
Their presence can be queried with UsdPrim::HasAPI.
ShapingAPI configures light emission shape, such as light cones and falloff.

question: Can I use shaders other than the physically-based UsdPreviewSurface, such as my own custom shaders, in USD materials?
expected_facts: UsdPreviewSurface models a physically-based surface.
Custom GLSLFX shaders can be used as nodes in a material network, set with info:glslfx:sourceAsset, and Hydra + Storm renders them.
Render contexts let one Material use different shader outputs for different renderers.

question: How can several submeshes with different materials share the same position, normal, and texture coordinate arrays within one mesh, instead of making a separate UsdGeomMesh for each submesh?
Why doesn't UsdGeomPrimvarsAPI::GetPrimvars() return primvars with extra namespaces like primvars:colorSet1:indices, and which method returns them?
Can I specify a tangent space on a UsdGeomMesh that affects normal mapping with a UsdPreviewSurface shader?
expected_facts: The material input frame:tangentsPrimvarName names the geometry primvar holding tangents (default "tangents").
frame:binormalsPrimvarName names the binormals primvar (default "binormals"), and frame:stPrimvarName names the texture coordinates used to compute the tangent frame.
Only one tangent frame is currently supported.

question: Can I communicate with or control a running usdview process, for example to make it reopen the stage?
How can I get the path of the material bound to a mesh prim using the Python usd-core package?
expected_facts: UsdShade.MaterialBindingAPI(prim).GetDirectBindingRel().GetTargets() returns the bound material's path.
The target is remapped into the stage's namespace, not the authored path.

question: usdc crate files use LZ4 compression. How do I enable the LZ4_HC variant to get better compression?
What do timeCodesPerSecond and framesPerSecond each represent?
expected_facts: timeCodesPerSecond scales TimeCode coordinates to real-time seconds.
framesPerSecond indicates the desired playback rate on playback devices and normally does not affect TimeCode scaling.
framesPerSecond is used as a fallback for timeCodesPerSecond only when timeCodesPerSecond is not set.

question: Should a camera's projection attribute be uniform, or are there cases where the projection needs to be animated?
Is authoring extent on gprims required, or are extents only optional hints?
expected_facts: Valid UsdGeom scene description should always provide an authored extent on a gprim.
If the gprim's shape is animated, the authored extent should capture the changing shape.
Extents are not automatically recomputed when geometry changes.

question: Does the explicitOnly expansion rule apply to expression-mode collections?
expected_facts: For a pattern-based (expression-mode) collection, explicitOnly is equivalent to expandPrims.
With expandPrims, only prims are tested against the membershipExpression; it is the default.

question: I keep my material assignments and geometry settings in a separate lookdev layer. Sublayering it works, but I can't get the same result with a reference. Are references mainly for bringing new things into the scene graph, while sublayers are for layering decisions like attribute changes?
expected_facts: SubLayers is the composition arc used to construct LayerStacks.
The primary use of references is composing smaller units of scene description into larger aggregates.
References can achieve similar layering only when one knows exactly which prims need to be layered.

question: I referenced set.usd under /shot/set, added a camera and saved the result as shot.usd with /shot as the default prim. When I reference shot.usd somewhere else, I get errors that set.usd can't be opened and that the explicit prim /root/shot is missing. Why does the second reference fail when the first one worked?
When I try to assign a new material to meshes inside a referenced USD model, I get the error 'Authoring to an instance proxy is not allowed'. What does this mean and how do I work around it?
expected_facts: Making a reference instanceable declares that no overrides will be expressed on prims beneath it; such overrides are ignored.
Instanceability can be overridden in a stronger layer (instanceable = false) to break the instance and get back its own children.
Collections authored outside instances can target prims inside instances (instance proxies) and be bound to materials.

question: Do prims inherit attributes or primvars from their parent prims? My id primvar is on the parent prim, but the geometry subsets where the shader is assigned don't see it. Should I copy the attribute down or look it up on the parent?
expected_facts: Regular attributes apply only to the prim on which they are specified.
Primvars also apply to child imageable prims unless those children have their own opinions.
Only constant-interpolation primvars are inherited down the namespace.

question: How do I rename a UV primvar, for example from 'UVMap' to 'uv', and how do I choose the interpolation when creating a new primvar?
expected_facts: UsdNamespaceEditor.MovePropertyAtPath renames a property; call ApplyEdits() to execute it.
UsdGeom.PrimvarsAPI.CreatePrimvar takes the interpolation as an argument after the type, e.g. UsdGeom.Tokens.varying.

question: I animated a material input by authoring time samples on it. It animates in one render delegate, but others only use the default value. What is the preferred way to animate material parameters in USD? Are primvars the only option?
When I bring a static Alembic model in through a sublayer or reference, time samples get written. How can I load it without writing any time samples?
How can I instance lights in USD? When I use an instancer for lights, they don't render.
Can I light-link, or exclude from shadow casting, individual sub-parts of point-instanced assets, such as a collection of tree branches? It only seems to work when the instances are plain references.
In a very heavy scene, how can I show a low-res proxy of the geometry in the viewport for set dressing but render the high-res version?
expected_facts: Give the low-res geometry purpose proxy and the high-res geometry purpose render.
Proxy-purpose prims are meant for lightweight renders and interactive viewports; render-purpose prims for final-quality renders.

question: Can one asset have both model variants and material variants, so I can choose 'cube' + 'red' or 'sphere' + 'blue', without adding lots of grouping prims or making a variant for every combination?
expected_facts: A prim can have an unlimited number of VariantSets declared directly on itself.
The final order of the VariantSets gives their relative strength if their opinions overlap.

question: My assembly file already has a 'model' variant set with v001 and v002. How do I add a v003 variant to that existing set without overwriting it, so the existing variants are kept?
expected_facts: Downstream contexts can dynamically add new variants to an existing VariantSet.
Author the new variant in a stronger layer; in that context both the existing and the new variants are available and selectable.

question: For large crowds, is it a sensible approach to cache per-frame USD files in parallel on a render farm and then stitch them together with value clips?
expected_facts: Value clips can stitch per-time-step generated/simulation assets into a continuous animation without impacting the generation process.
usdstitchclips assembles a sequence of file-per-time-step layers into a Value Clips representation.

question: How do I set up a looping animation on a referenced USD asset with value clips, so I can scatter offset variations of it?
expected_facts: Use an explicit clip set: its times list of (stageTime, clipTime) pairs can scale, offset and loop clips.
Templated clip sets do not support looping.
For example, times = [(0, 0), (10, 10), (10, 0), (20, 10)] plays the clip twice.

question: How can I flatten a layer's own sublayers (its layer stack) into a single layer?
expected_facts: Use UsdUtilsFlattenLayerStack.
Or use usdcat with the --flattenLayerStack option.

question: What units are USD camera aperture values in? Entering a 36x24 mm aperture gives a broken field of view, and I need values about 100 times larger to get the expected result.
expected_facts: Aperture and focal length use the same units, treated as 1/10 of the scene's world unit.
With centimeter world units they are millimeters; with other world units you may have to adjust.

question: If I bring geometry modeled with a different up axis into my stage, does the stage's upAxis correct it automatically?
expected_facts: The up axis is declared in the root layer's stage metadata and applies to all Xformable objects, including referenced geometry.
If objects were modeled with mixed up axes, you may need to apply a corrective transform.

question: How do collection-based material bindings work? Which prim should own the collection and the binding relationship? I get errors like 'Can only append a property material:binding:collection:spheres to a prim path'.
expected_facts: A material:binding:collection:NAME relationship can be authored on any prim and must target a single Material and a single Collection.
It binds the Material to the collection's prims that live beneath the prim holding the binding relationship.

question: Can I control the order of a render product's render vars instead of relying on alphabetical order?
expected_facts: The RenderProduct orderedVars relationship lists the RenderVars combined into the product.
If ordering matters to the output driver, the order of targets in orderedVars is used.

question: In a Python script, how can I work with a stage's composed prims while directing my edits into one specific layer?
expected_facts: Use an Edit Target (UsdEditTarget) to choose which layer receives the opinions authored through composed prims.
Set it with UsdStage::SetEditTarget or a UsdEditContext.

question: Is there a rule about hyphens in primvar names? My material's texture reader uses a varname with hyphens, like 'Cube_001-mesh-map-0', but the mesh's primvar has underscores instead. Is it safe to always convert hyphens to underscores when looking up primvars?
With the pxr Python package, how do I list all the attributes of a Usd.Prim? dir() and vars() only return methods.
expected_facts: GetPropertyNames() lists a prim's property names.
GetAttributes() returns the prim's UsdAttribute objects (GetProperties and GetRelationships return properties and relationships).

question: How do I make a polygon with a hole in USD without splitting it into convex pieces or triangulating? holeIndices only hides the inner face and doesn't cut it out of the outer polygon.

How do I put a custom C++ struct into a VtValue, not for serialization but to pass it through Hydra? I implemented hash_value and operator==, but I get 'Unsupported type' and can't read the struct back.
How do I create a USDZ file? I couldn't find the details in the USDZ file format documentation.
expected_facts: Use usdzip; with --asset (or --arkitAsset) it localizes the USD file and the files it references, then creates a new usdz package.
UsdUtilsCreateNewUsdzPackage does the same localizing and packaging from the API.

question: I unzipped a USDZ file to change a texture, but when I zip it again (no compression, no encryption) it no longer works, even without any changes. Is there a special way to repackage a USDZ?
expected_facts: Each file's data must begin at a multiple of 64 bytes from the start of the package.
Off-the-shelf zip tools cannot set that alignment, so USD provides its own packaging tool (usdzip).
The first file must be a native USD file for the package to open on a stage as is.

question: Is there a Python or command-line tool that validates whether a generated USDZ file is correct?
expected_facts: usdchecker validates USD and usdz files.
For usdz files, usdchecker --arkit enforces stricter web-compliant rules.
usdzip can optionally validate the contents as they are packaged.

question: In my exported USD file, the parent Xform prims have their transforms, but the transforms don't seem to apply to their child spheres when I view the file in usdview. Is that correct behavior? Shouldn't child prims inherit their parents' transforms?
expected_facts: Yes: a prim's local-to-world transform is the concatenation of its own local transformation with those of its ancestors.
